- Title: Bidirectional codification as a comparative test
- Description: Proposal: promote bidirectional codification from design guidance to a comparative conjecture, tested by evolving the same task stream under natural-language-only, symbolic-only, one-way promotion, and bidirectional codify-and-relax regimes

The guidance embeds a comparative claim nobody has tested — that the *bidirectionality* is load-bearing, not just prudent. The conjecture, stated so it can lose:

## `kb/sources/dreamcoder-wake-sleep-bayesian-program-learning.ingest.md`

- Title: Ingest: DreamCoder: growing interpretable knowledge with wake-sleep Bayesian program learning
- Description: DreamCoder grows a symbolic library under a description-length gate; lands as the middle case between ungated and proof-gated self-improvement, and the formal-domain limit of mechanical abstraction

> The gate is also a proxy the paper does not separate from what it stands in for. Description length is measured over already-solved training programs; nothing in the criterion sees held-out generalization. Held-out performance is reported and is good, but the causal link from "shortens the training corpus" to "transfers" is asserted by correlation (the r=0.79 depth-performance figure) rather than isolated by an ablation that varies the gate while holding search fixed. The baselines compare against weaker search (enumeration, exploration-compression, RobustFill on the initial library) and against memorization, but not against a strong human-authored DSL for the same domain -- the comparison that would tell us whether learned libraries beat expert-designed ones, which is the question [codification and relaxing navigate the bitter lesson boundary](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) actually cares about.

## `kb/sources/duguid-on-rereading-suchman-situated-action.ingest.md`

- Title: Ingest: On rereading. Suchman and Situated Action
- Description: Duguid 2012 rereads Suchman: plans are interpreted resources, not controllers of action; conformity pressure hides plan gaps; scale can disguise principled limits as practical ones

> The Moore's Law frame **compares with** [codification and relaxing navigate the bitter lesson boundary](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) and [the bitter lesson selects against unearned reach](../theory/bitter-lesson-selects-against-unearned-reach-not-against-structure.md). The shared axis is whether a limitation can be identified as compute-curable before scale tests it. The first note says it cannot. Duguid poses the same identification problem from the critic's side, but in 2012 he asserted that natural-language failures were principled, and later LLM progress partly tests that example. The Heideggerian premise he relays ("implicit assumptions cannot all be made explicit") **compares with** [Naur's human-only conclusion](../theory/naur-equates-machine-execution-with-formulated-criteria.md). Both lines of thought need an extra premise to move from inexplicit practical understanding to human-only competence. Finally, the routinization case **compares with** [Argyris on organizational learning and MIS](./argyris-organizational-learning-and-mis-1977.ingest.md), where tighter control induces ritual compliance, and with [Norman's account of si [cut at 1200 characters]

## `kb/sources/from-entropy-to-epiplexity-rethinking-information-computational.ingest.md`

- Title: Ingest: From Entropy to Epiplexity: Rethinking Information for Computationally Bounded Intelligence
- Description: Epiplexity paper formalizing extractable structure for computationally bounded observers, useful for observer-relative information value and context-efficiency theory.

> The connect report found seven direct connections. The central one is [information value is observer-relative](../theory/information-value-is-observer-relative.md): the paper gives the note a formal ML-facing measure for pattern extractability under bounded computation and explains why deterministic restructuring can create usable information for a bounded consumer even when it adds no classical information. The paper also grounds [reverse compression](../theory/reverse-compression-is-when-llm-output-expands-without-adding.md) by supplying a candidate measure for whether expanded prose adds extractable structure. It enables [minimum viable vocabulary](../theory/minimum-viable-vocabulary-is-the-naming-set-that-most-reduces.md), because prequential or requential coding could test whether a vocabulary makes more domain structure accessible. It extends [codification and relaxing navigate the bitter lesson boundary](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) by offering a way to reason about whether an extracted regularity is genuine learnable structure or an observer-relative artifact. Finally, it grounds [context efficiency](../theory/context-efficienc [cut at 1200 characters]

> 6. **Codification bets can be described as bets on durable structure** -- Epiplexity gives [codification and relaxing](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) a sharper distinction: codify regularities that are stable learnable structure, stay cautious around apparent patterns that only current observers can cheaply see. This is useful as a conceptual check, not yet an engineering rule. [just-a-reference]

## `kb/sources/induction-bias-sequence-models-ebrahimi-2026.ingest.md`

- Title: Ingest: On the "Induction Bias" in Sequence Models
- Description: 190k-run empirical study showing transformers need orders-of-magnitude more data than RNNs for state tracking due to absence of step-by-step induction bias; introduces sharing factor kappa quantifying cross-length mechanism reuse

> - [codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) -- **grounds**: Step-by-step decomposition is a permanent architectural advantage for state tracking, not a temporary one that scale dissolves. The kappa results show that the general method (transformer) not only fails to scale past the constraint -- it actively degrades (destructive interference) when exposed to more diverse data.

## `kb/sources/no-free-lunch-theorem-no-universal-learning-algorithm.ingest.md`

- Title: Ingest: The No Free Lunch Theorem
- Description: No Free Lunch explainer grounding codification as an unavoidable inductive-bias bet: strategies win only when their assumptions match the problem distribution.

> The connect report found the strongest fit in the KB's fixed-artifact and codify/relax cluster. The source is evidence for [fixed artifacts split into exact specs and proxy theories](../theory/exact-implementation-does-not-validate-a-requirement.md), because it explains why local wins imply hidden assumptions about the problem distribution. It also supports [codification and relaxing navigate the bitter lesson boundary](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md): every codified strategy is an inductive-bias bet that improves reliability, speed, or cost only where the world matches its assumptions. The A-star hopper example gives [operational signals that a component is a relaxing candidate](../theory/operational-signals-that-a-component-is-a-relaxing-candidate.md) a simple distribution-shift exhibit, and the final "assumptions match the world" framing supports [specification strategy should follow where understanding lives](../theory/specification-strategy-should-follow-where-understanding-lives.md).

> Update [codification and relaxing navigate the bitter lesson boundary](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md): add a short paragraph in "Every codification is a bet" using No Free Lunch to state the general form of the bet. A codified artifact is an inductive bias over problem distributions; it earns reliability/speed/cost gains where its assumptions match the world and becomes a relaxing candidate where they do not. Cite this source as the accessible explainer, while preserving Wolpert/Macready or Ho/Pepyne as the formal theorem lineage if a formal citation is needed.

## `kb/sources/symbols-neural-networks-mathematical-intelligence.ingest.md`

- Title: Ingest: Symbols, neural networks, and mathematical intelligence
- Description: Lampinen reads the IMO Lean-to-natural-language shift and LLM conjecture disproofs as connectionist vindication: symbol systems are learned external tools, not intelligence

> The IMO sequence is the first formal-reasoning instance in the KB's bitter-lesson cluster. It illustrates the absorption half of [scaling absorbs scaffolding at fixed task difficulty, not at the deployment frontier](../theory/scaling-absorbs-scaffolding-at-fixed-difficulty-not-at-the-frontier.md) (is-evidence-for). Olympiad problems stay fixed in difficulty while the Lean scaffold disappears across model generations. The note's "Observed at both ends" section currently has only practitioner cases. The case also illustrates relaxing in [codification and relaxing navigate the bitter lesson boundary](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) (is-evidence-for), whose examples come from vision and hardware. In both uses the comparison changes the model, training, compute, and reasoning medium together. It therefore illustrates absorption and does not isolate the removal of the formal constraint as the cause. The essay is silent on the frontier-recurrence half of the scaling note: it says solvers "may" have been used for the conjecture results and sets that aside.

## `kb/sources/the-anatomy-of-an-agent-harness-2031408954517971368.ingest.md`

- Title: Ingest: The Anatomy of an Agent Harness
- Description: Practitioner taxonomy deriving harness components (filesystem, bash, sandboxes, memory, context management, long-horizon execution) from model limitations — provides the component anatomy that bridges Lopopolo's practice and the cybernetics framing

> - [codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) — **exemplifies**: the model/harness co-training feedback loop is codify/relax operating at the training boundary

> 2. **No engagement with what harness components should be *removed*.** The post is entirely additive — each section adds a component. But the [Voooooogel "What Survives" source](voooooogel-multi-agent-future.ingest.md) argues that many harness components are vision features that stronger models will dissolve. The post acknowledges this in one sentence ("some of what lives in the harness today will get absorbed into the model") but doesn't identify *which* components are candidates for absorption. The [codification-and-relaxing](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) framework provides the analytical tool (arithmetic regime components survive, vision-feature components relax), but this source doesn't use it or anything equivalent.

> Write a note titled "Practitioner harness taxonomy converges on KB theoretical framework" connecting to [methodology-enforcement-is-constraining](../theory/methodology-enforcement-is-constraining.md), [codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md), and [context-efficiency-is-the-central-design-concern-in-agent-systems](../theory/context-efficiency-is-the-central-design-concern-in-agent-systems.md) — it would argue that three independent sources (Vtrivedy10's component taxonomy, Lopopolo's practitioner report, the cybernetics thread) describe the same phenomena the KB's theoretical notes name (constraining, codify/relax, context efficiency, deploy-time learning), and that this convergence from practice onto theory is evidence the framework captures something real. The note would include a mapping table: harness component -> model limitation it addresses -> KB concept it instantiates. This fills the synthesis opportunity flagged by `/connect`: the KB has the theories and the practitioner evidence, but no note yet explicitly maps between them.

## `kb/sources/voooooogel-multi-agent-future.ingest.md`

- Title: Ingest: What Survives in Multi-Agent Systems
- Description: Applied bitter-lesson analysis predicting which multi-agent patterns survive stronger models — argues filesystem, forking, and spawning are structural while fixed orchestration is a vision feature

> **Grounding the KB's learning-theory cluster.** The source's entire argument is an applied [bitter-lesson-boundary](../theory/exact-implementation-does-not-validate-a-requirement.md) analysis: filesystem and multi-agent parallelism survive because they're structural (spec IS the problem), while fixed role hierarchies are vision features (theories about how to organize agents). It directly exemplifies the [codification-and-relaxing](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) framework — current orchestration patterns are codifications that will relax when scale makes model-discovered decompositions viable. Specific relaxing signals from the [relaxing-signals](../theory/operational-signals-that-a-component-is-a-relaxing-candidate.md) catalogue are identifiable in the source's examples.

## `kb/sources/what-is-an-agent-harness-2046980769747533830.ingest.md`

- Title: Ingest: What is an Agent Harness
- Description: Arize taxonomy separates nine harness components and adds permission/safety plus lifecycle hooks as first-class primitives, a fifth independent convergence on the harness decomposition

> 4. **Harness-vs-framework as the bottom-up vs. top-down inversion.** The polemical move ("frameworks are configured by humans; harnesses ship as working agents") is the same inversion the bitter-lesson notes ([codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md)) describe at the model-substrate level, now restated at the runtime-architecture level. Frameworks let the human do the configuration work that ought to be deferred to the model and the convergent architecture. Connects to the [Mismanaged Geniuses ingest](./the-mismanaged-geniuses-hypothesis-2042588627260018751.ingest.md). [experiment]

> 2. **No engagement with what survives or what should be removed.** The taxonomy is entirely additive -- every section adds a component. But the [codification-and-relaxing](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) framework predicts that some current harness components will be absorbed into the model (e.g., context management, file-selection heuristics) while others will persist (e.g., permission enforcement). Dhinakaran's "push decisions to the model" gestures at this but does not identify *which* components are candidates for absorption. Same gap noted in the Vtrivedy10 ingest.

> Write a note titled "Permission and safety form a non-pushable layer beneath the agent loop" connecting to [methodology-enforcement-is-constraining](../theory/methodology-enforcement-is-constraining.md), [agent-runtimes-decompose-into-scheduler-context-engine-and-execution-substrate](../theory/agent-runtime-analysis-should-separate-scheduling-context-state.md), and [codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary](../theory/codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) -- it would argue that the permission/safety layer is the canonical example of a decision that *cannot* be pushed to the model, and that distinguishing **judgment-pushable** from **safety-codified** decisions is what the "push decisions to the model" maturation pattern actually means. Dhinakaran's nine-component spec (permission tiers, dynamic command classification, allow/deny rules, interactive approval) and Lopopolo's structural-tests-as-permissions provide two practitioner sources; the note would name the bifurcation that resolves the apparent tension between "push to model" and "enforce beneath model" as two facets of the same maturation. This addresses the gap flagged in the co [cut at 1200 characters]

- Title: The bitter lesson selects against unearned reach, not against structure
- Description: The lesson selects against claims whose reach was asserted rather than earned by a refuting test, not against structure or origin — theory search in readable forms is its own method; earned reach protects the claim, not its carrier

## `kb/theory/codify-versus-llm-decision-heuristics.md`

- Title: Codify-versus-LLM decision heuristics
- Description: Specification, checking, permitted interpretations, repeated-use cost, and the stake set against a pattern's stated odds and exposure inform which operations to codify; none alone makes code or model interpretation universally preferable

> The repetition comparison above prices a conversion that is assumed to
> hold. A conversion is also a bet that the extracted pattern is part of the
> task rather than an accident of the observed cases
> ([codification is a bet](./codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md)).
> Two further terms follow from treating it as one, and the KB's own record
> shows decisions that went wrong for lack of them.

> A codified operation is a [relaxation
> candidate](./codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md)
> when its assumptions repeatedly fail or its maintenance cost exceeds an
> adequate alternative. Growing exceptions and integration failures are prompts

## `kb/theory/continual-learning-requires-governing-behaviour-changing-writes.md`

- Title: Continual learning requires governing behaviour-changing writes, not just storing content
- Description: For deployed systems, persistence is insufficient; continual learning must select, validate, authorize, and coordinate behaviour-changing updates across the representational forms a system can change

> The resulting problem is governance: autonomously *choosing* a behaviour-changing write, *validating* it against open-ended behaviour, assigning it an authority path, and coordinating it with other retained parts of the system. Form placement is itself revisable. A stable natural-language rule may be codified, while a brittle symbolic rule may be relaxed back into prose ([codification and relaxing](./codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md)). Mature release engineering already governs hand-authored readable changes, and not every governed write is learning. A behaviour-changing write counts as continual learning when the system's own loop selects and retains it because deployment evidence bears on an improvement objective — for retained candidates, search, reject-capable evaluation, and operative retention ([a proposal-selection improvement loop](./a-proposal-selection-loop-requires-search-evaluation-and-retention.md)). The same edit hand-authored in reaction to an incident is maintenance, however durable and behaviour-changing. Continual-learning systems must close that evidence-responsive loop at the cadence their environment requires. Storage, [contextua [cut at 1200 characters]

## `kb/theory/definitions/codification.md`

- Title: Codification
- Description: Definition — moves a natural-language rule into symbolic form by rewriting it or adopting a consumer as its governing reference; conformance does not establish task adequacy.

> [Progressive constraining](../progressive-constraining-commits-only-after-patterns-stabilize.md) commits a pattern to code once observed runs show it is stable; committing a single LLM output instead fixes an arbitrary reading. How far codification can go depends on the available checks: [hard oracles make it easier, weak oracles resist it](../oracle-strength-spectrum.md). Every codification is a bet that the committed reading stays right. [Relaxing](../codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) reverses the codification when the reading turns out to be a wrong proxy, or when a more general component handles the case well enough.

> - [codification and relaxing navigate the bitter-lesson boundary](../codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) — extends: when to reverse a codification

## `kb/theory/definitions/constraining.md`

- Title: Constraining
- Description: Definition — constraining commits choices in a retained artifact that narrow which readings or behaviors its consumer should treat as valid, or rank the valid ones; codification settles by fixed rules what natural language leaves open

> **Relaxing** is the reverse: replacing a constrained component with a more general one so interpretation space reopens. It is warranted when the committed reading turns out to be a wrong proxy, or when a more capable consumer handles the general case well enough. See [codification and relaxing navigate the bitter-lesson boundary](../codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) and [operational signals that a component is a relaxing candidate](../operational-signals-that-a-component-is-a-relaxing-candidate.md).

> - [codification and relaxing navigate the bitter-lesson boundary](../codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) — extends: when to relax

## `kb/theory/definitions/representational-form.md`

- Title: Representational form
- Description: Definition — classifies content by path-relative localization and a governing semantic reference; opacity separately describes affordable inspection.

> Moves between forms are named operations: [codification](./codification.md) moves content from natural-language into symbolic form, by rewriting it or by adopting a consumer as its reference; [relaxing](../codification-and-relaxing-navigate-the-bitter-lesson-boundary.md) replaces a constrained component with a more general one; and training moves content into distributed-parametric form.

description: Since you can't identify which side of the bitter lesson boundary you're on until scale tests it, practical systems must codify and relax — with spec mining avoiding the vision-feature failure mode

# Codification and relaxing navigate the bitter lesson boundary

The [fixed-artifact distinction](./exact-implementation-does-not-validate-a-requirement.md) separates exact specs (the spec is the problem) from proxy theories (the spec is a theory about a larger capability). Since you can't reliably tell which regime you're in until scale tests the distinction, practical systems will always be hybrids — combining explicit scripts and checks with learned components. This is not a partition into codified versus learned: an adopted model package can itself be a codified reference.

## The trade-off depends on which regime you're in

[Codification](./definitions/codification.md) moves a rule or operation into symbolic form by rewriting it or adopting a governing reference. This note concerns the code-extraction case: committing an interpreted rule to a script, executable test, schema, or validator whose behavior can be inspected and checked at acceptable cost. Retaining a prose convention alone is not codification. Adopting a model package can codify an operation without providing this case's readable rules or reducing inference cost.

Code extraction can [trade generality for gains in reliability, speed, and cost](./constraining-and-extraction-both-trade-generality-for-reliability.md) when the committed procedure fits and its execution and maintenance are cheaper than repeated interpretation. But such a procedure can also encode a decomposition of a larger problem, and the arithmetic/vision-feature boundary determines what capability the commitment risks excluding:

- **Arithmetic-regime decompositions**: the spec fully captures the subproblem, so implementing it need not lose generality within that declared scope. An inspectable script or validator can improve reliability, speed, and cost without excluding required behavior; the economic gain still depends on implementation and maintenance costs.
- **Vision-feature decompositions**: the spec is a plausible theory of a larger capability, so an efficient local implementation can lose generality at that larger scope. When scale makes the general approach good enough on reliability, speed, and cost, that loss may no longer be worth it.

Code extraction therefore has a complement: **relaxing** — replacing an extracted component with a more general one, often a model call, when scale makes that viable, accepting higher cost and lower reliability in exchange for regaining generality. The replacement can itself be codified by adoption; what relaxing reverses is the extraction, not symbolic membership.

The trajectory runs in both directions, and can repeat at different levels of the stack. Edge detection was codified (hand-coded algorithms), relaxed (replaced by learned features), and may re-codify as an accelerator inside a learned architecture. FlashAttention is hand-crafted algorithmic optimization embedded within learned architectures; tokenizers are engineered preprocessing that learned models depend on. The bitter lesson describes a trajectory, not a law of nature.

## Every code-extraction codification is a bet

In this case codification extracts a regularity and commits it to code. The bet is that what you extracted is genuinely part of the spec — load-bearing behavior that the system needs — rather than an accidental pattern that happens to hold on observed data. That is the same property [one case-level conjecture offers as the diagnosis of a structured method's loss under scaling](./bitter-lesson-selects-against-unearned-reach-not-against-structure.md), seen from the author's side rather than the survivor's: a codification that commits an accident asserts a scope that nothing assessed, and relaxing is what happens to it later. That scale in fact selects on this property is conjectural, not established.

In the arithmetic regime, the bet is safe: the spec IS the problem, and the solution is algorithmically determined. In the vision-feature regime, the bet is risky: the spec is a theory, and scale may reveal a better path. Most practical codification happens in the blurry zone between them, where you can't tell which regime you're in.

The vision researchers made this bet at maximum disadvantage. They formalized subproblems — edge detection, corner detection — without a working "seeing" system to extract from. They were betting that theorized components would compose into the target capability, with no evidence of successful composition.

[Spec mining](./spec-mining-as-codification.md) improves the odds by starting from a working system. You watch a system that already achieves the target behavior (however unreliably), identify regularities, and extract those into formal checks. The bet shifts from "will these pieces compose?" (which the vision researchers lost) to "is this specific pattern load-bearing?" — a narrower bet with better odds, because you've already observed the behavior composing successfully.

But it's still a bet. A mined spec might capture an accidental regularity — a pattern that holds on the observed data but isn't what makes the system work. [Relaxing signals](./operational-signals-that-a-component-is-a-relaxing-candidate.md) are how you detect a losing bet: distribution shift, paraphrase brittleness, and isolation-vs-integration gaps reveal when a codified component encodes an accident rather than a spec.

Two formal results help bound when codification bets are safe. The epiplexity framework ([Finzi et al., 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.03220v1)) separates information into time-bounded entropy (irreducible randomness) and epiplexity (learnable structure within computational bounds). High-epiplexity regularities are genuinely structural — codifying them is safer because they reflect real patterns, not artefacts of the observer's computational budget. Low-epiplexity patterns that appear regular may be accidents visible only at current scale.

The induction bias results ([Ebrahimi et al., 2026](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.18333)) provide evidence from the other direction: for calculator-class state tracking, architectural induction bias (step-by-step decomposition) is a permanent advantage, not a temporary one that scale dissolves. Transformers show sharing factor κ ≈ 1 or κ < 1 across all supervision formats — they learn length-specific solutions in isolation, with training diversity actively hurting (κ = 0.28 for CoT). This means codification bets in the arithmetic regime are not merely safe-for-now; the step-by-step structure that codification encodes is the kind of regularity that persists under scaling.

## Working heuristics

1. **Codify for current leverage, not permanence.** An executable test that checks "does this function return the right number" is in the arithmetic regime relative to that numerical contract. A workflow that enforces "always decompose agents into these three phases" is probably a vision feature relative to broader task success. Both can be codified — but expect the second kind to eventually relax. Merely writing the convention in natural language constrains without codifying it.

2. **Prefer specs that describe what over how.** The more a codified artifact encodes a theory of how something works (rather than what it should produce), the more likely it is a relaxing candidate. "This endpoint returns X given Y" survives longer than "always process requests in three stages."

3. **Watch for composition failure as a relaxing signal.** If codified conventions don't compose into better systems, that's the signal to relax — replace the rigid decomposition with a more general one.

---

Sources:
- Finzi et al. (2026). [From entropy to epiplexity](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.03220v1) — formal framework distinguishing learnable structure from observer-relative artefacts; grounds when codification targets real patterns.
- Ebrahimi et al. (2026). [On the "induction bias" in sequence models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.18333) — 190K training runs showing architectural induction bias is permanent for calculator-class tasks; codification bets in the arithmetic regime persist under scaling.

Relevant Notes:

- [Unsupported proxy scope may explain a structured method's loss under scaling](./bitter-lesson-selects-against-unearned-reach-not-against-structure.md) — grounds: the case-level diagnosis this note reads from the author's side; it conjectures what may determine the outcome without establishing it or restoring the foresight this note denies
- [fixed artifacts split into exact specs and proxy theories](./exact-implementation-does-not-validate-a-requirement.md) — foundation: the exact-spec/proxy-theory distinction this note operationalizes
- [the verifiability gradient](./verifiability-gradient.md) — grounds: available checks guide whether to extract a rule into a script or validator
- [constraining and extraction can trade generality for reliability, speed, or cost](./constraining-and-extraction-both-trade-generality-for-reliability.md) — grounds: the trade-off code-extraction codification can enact
- [spec mining as codification](./spec-mining-as-codification.md) — the bottom-up extraction method that avoids the vision-feature failure mode
- [relaxing signals](./operational-signals-that-a-component-is-a-relaxing-candidate.md) — detects when codified components are encoding vision features

---
description: Report method that states a note's role in the KB from the passages that link to it, and reports what its dependents need, what it duplicates, which recommendations it has not taken up, and whom a change would reach
type: types/instruction.md
depth: 1
---

# Report a note's role in the KB

A note's text does not show what the KB uses it for. Other notes cite it for a term, a premise or a distinction. Source ingests recommend changes to it. A local repair that looks right inside the note can break a dependent, or miss that a dependent already states the claim better. This method reads the note together with the passages that link to it and reports the note's role. "Gate" is its file name only: it is **not a catalog gate** and gives no verdict. It is a report criterion, and its result is the **role report**. Write the report; do not touch the note.

## Inputs

- The note.
- `inbound`: the note's inbound contexts. For each file under `kb/` that links to the note, outside `kb/reports/` and `kb/work/`, it gives the file's repository path, title and description, and each passage that holds a link to the note. The text says when a cap cut files or passages. When nothing links to the note, it says so.

Judge only from these inputs. Do not open the linking files, and do not search for other links. A file or passage the caps cut is unseen: name the cut where it limits a finding.

It runs alone, with no other criterion:

```bash
commonplace-review NOTE --criteria role
commonplace-review NOTE --criteria role --input inbound=PATH
```

Without `--input`, the command collects the inbound contexts itself. The run keeps its result as a retained observation and writes no current result, because no freshness hash covers the inbound contexts. The full improvement procedure (`commonplace-revise NOTE --full`) runs it after its review sweep and hands the report to the assessor.

## The hard rule

Propose nothing about how to edit the note or its dependents. Do not rank edits, draft replacement text or recommend a pass. The product is a description of the note's role and of the dependencies a change would meet. Whoever plans the edit decides what to do with it.

## What to report

1. **Role.** In two or three sentences, state what the note is for in the KB as its dependents use it. Examples: it supplies a vocabulary pair that three notes cite; it is a premise other notes argue from; only tag heads cite it, and no dependent argues from it; nothing links to it. Then write one line that names the note's terms and claims that dependents rely on, and the ones no dependent uses.
2. **Dependents.** For each linking file, say what it needs from the note: a term, a claim, a distinction, a premise, or only a citation. Say whether the note supplies it: `SUPPLIED`, `PARTLY SUPPLIED` or `NOT SUPPLIED`. A dependent that uses a term in another sense than the note's does not get what it needs.
3. **Duplication.** Report where the note restates what a dependent's passage already states, or where a dependent restates the note. Say which states it better for the dependents' use, and why, when the passages show it.
4. **Untaken recommendations.** A linking source can recommend a change to the note: an ingest's "recommended next action", a "revise" or "add this citation" passage. Compare each with the note's text. Report each recommendation the note has not taken up. Report one the note has taken up only when it is partly taken up.
5. **Reach.** Name the claims and terms whose change would reach dependents, and name those dependents. A change to a claim or term that no dependent uses reaches no one; say so. Do not recommend cutting content because no dependent uses it. The report says who uses the note, not whether its claims are good theory; a sound claim can precede its dependents.

## Output

The caller names the output file. Write only that file; mutate nothing else. The output is a [review result](../types/review-result.md) fragment with `outcome: report` and no `attack-outcome`.

Each dependent need, each duplication and each untaken recommendation is one finding. Begin its `reason` with `SUPPLIED`, `PARTLY SUPPLIED`, `NOT SUPPLIED`, `DUPLICATED` or `UNTAKEN`, then name the linking file's repository path and state the need, overlap or recommendation. Give `scope: passage` with a quote from the note when one span of the note carries what the dependent relies on; otherwise give `scope: document` with no quotes. A note that nothing links to has no findings.

Keep `## Role` first and self-contained: a later reader may receive that section alone.

```markdown
---
type: types/review-result.md
findings:
  - scope: passage
    quotes: ["<the span of the note the dependent relies on>"]
    reason: "PARTLY SUPPLIED — <linking file path> — <what it needs and what is missing>"
outcome: report
---

# Role in the KB: <note title>

## Role
<two or three sentences: what the note is for, as its dependents use it>
Relied on: <terms and claims>. Unused: <terms and claims no dependent uses>.

## Dependents
<one line per linking file: its path and what it needs; the needs themselves are the findings>

## Duplication
<the overlaps, or "None">

## Untaken recommendations
<the recommendations not taken up, or "None">

## Reach
<the claims and terms a change would carry to dependents, with the dependents named, or "No dependent relies on the note's claims or terms">
```

contracts.types/review-result.md:
---
type: types/type-spec.md
name: review-result
description: "One completed gate, conformance or report-method assessment with structured findings and controller-owned execution provenance"
schema: ./review-result.schema.yaml
---

# Review result

A review result records one assessment of captured target text against a criterion. Completion means the output passed deterministic checks, not that its judgment is correct. A report outcome is not a favorable verdict. Use this type for individual gate, compression-check, type-conformance and collection-conformance verdicts, and for critique, composition-friction, premise-decomposition and compression-synthesis reports and role reports. Do not use it for combined improvement packets or connection discovery.

## Content

Findings state what the assessed text establishes or fails to establish. Each passage finding quotes enough verbatim text to identify one contiguous span uniquely. A quote is matched after whitespace and typographic quote marks are normalized, so a line wrap in the target does not break it. A quote therefore identifies a passage and is not a byte-exact copy of it. A consumer that needs the exact span locates the quote in the captured target, which holds the exact bytes. A document-wide or absence finding explains the condition without inventing a quotation. Finding levels belong to verdict criteria; critique reports instead state whether the strongest attack lands and how the note engages it. An empty findings list is an honest completed result when no finding remains.

The body explains the assessment without repeating every structured finding. A critique preserves its central commitment, critique mode, strongest case, the note's response and constructive findings, including why an attack does not survive. Low-confidence no-surviving-attack findings leave the need for a domain check visible.

Each report method has its own shape, which the schema checks by the result's `criterion`:

| Method | Findings | Required body |
|---|---|---|
| Critique | constructive findings | `attack-outcome` in frontmatter; `## Strongest case against it`, `## How the note engages it`, `## Constructive findings` |
| Composition friction | the surfaced joints, thinnest first; each reason begins `UNSUPPORTED`, `THIN` or `HOLDS` | a `**Filter:** SURVIVES` or `DISSOLVES` line; `## Filter`, `## Thinnest joints`, `## For the human` |
| Premise decomposition | one per premise; each reason begins `HOLDS`, `DOUBTFUL` or `DEFEATED`, and a non-`HOLDS` reason names `LOCAL` or `GLOBAL` and `instance`, `prevalence` or `priced-exception` | a `**Register:**` line; `## Premises and counterexamples`, `## For the human` |
| Compression synthesis | zero to three opportunities | `## Opportunities` |
| Role report | one per dependent need, duplication or untaken recommendation; each reason begins `SUPPLIED`, `PARTLY SUPPLIED`, `NOT SUPPLIED`, `DUPLICATED` or `UNTAKEN` | `## Role`, `## Dependents`, `## Duplication`, `## Untaken recommendations`, `## Reach` |

Only critique supplies `attack-outcome`. Friction's filter line and the premise statuses route attention; they are not overall verdicts. A report criterion is named by its library instruction's identity, so moving one of these instructions requires a schema edit.

## Field ownership

The worker fragment supplies only `type`, `findings`, `outcome`, optional `attack-outcome`, and the body. Findings precede the outcome so the serialized verdict follows its rationale. The fragment is not a complete saved artifact. The controller completes and validates it; workers never assert hashes, execution identities or timestamps.

| Fields | Owner and meaning |
|---|---|
| `type`, `findings`, `outcome`, `attack-outcome` | Worker assessment; findings contain `scope`, `quotes`, `reason`, and `level` for verdicts |
| `description`, `format`, `contract` | Controller's result-format identity and expected verdict/report contract |
| `note`, `criterion` | Original target and criterion identities |
| `note-sha256`, `criterion-sha256` | Freshness hashes; the note hash may cover normalized watched parts, not exact bytes |
| `target-sha256`, `target-capture` | Exact assessed UTF-8 bytes and their retained repository-relative location |
| `observation`, `contract-sha256` | Execution observation and captured output-contract identity |
| `profile`, `model`, `run`, `launch`, `completed-at` | Requested execution configuration and observed execution provenance |
| `raw-output`, `raw-output-sha256` | Retained original worker fragment, distinct from this completed artifact |

## Template

Worker fragment for a verdict criterion; code supplies the remaining fields:

```markdown
---
type: types/review-result.md
findings:
  - scope: document
    quotes: []
    reason: "The claim omits the condition needed for its stated conclusion."
    level: warn
outcome: warn
---

# Review

## Summary

The conclusion needs its missing condition.
```

A critique fragment uses `outcome: report`, supplies `attack-outcome`, and omits finding levels. Its body retains the critique instruction's sections. Other report fragments use `outcome: report`, omit `attack-outcome` and finding levels, and follow their instruction's Output section. Neither fragment uses a terminal `## Result:` line. Operational production and publication belong to the review command, not to this type.

type: types/collection-contract.md

# Writing conventions for kb/reports/ (report collection)

## Purpose and scope

This collection contains analytical outputs, evaluation records, and local
operational evidence that are consumed as reports rather than as library
claims or system definitions. Placement here is justified by the output's
retention policy and consumer, not by its filename or by the fact that a tool
generated it.

A report belongs here only when a named operation consumes the report itself.
Transferable claims belong in `kb/theory/`; descriptions of the shipped system
and its decisions belong in `kb/reference/`; executable procedures belong in
`kb/instructions/`; and reasoning whose value is consumed by unfinished work
belongs in `kb/work/`.

## Policy areas

Every report artifact lives in exactly one first-level policy area:

| Area | Retention policy | Typical contents |
|---|---|---|
| `state/` | Ignored, one directory per producing workflow. Not disposable merely because it was generated: the owning workflow decides when an output may be removed, and the [state README](./state/README.md) states per workflow what deletion loses. | Review results, packets and runs; fix dispositions; ingest working directories; connect, critique, friction, premise-decomposition and promotion-candidate reports. |
| `retained/` | Durable report records kept with the project. Payloads are tracked. | Evaluation corpora, experiment reports, measurements, and exact records cited by later work. |
| `types/` | Collection-local structural contracts, not report payloads. | Optional project-authored report contracts; command-produced generic report types are global. |

The published site includes `retained/` and leaves out `state/`. Inside `retained/`, a subtree carrying a
`.commonplace-validation-ignore` marker is left out of the site as well as
validation; mark exact captures and trial bundles so, keeping the report that
interprets them published.

Do not put report payloads directly at the collection root. Moving an artifact
between policy areas is a change in its retention contract, not a filing-only
rename.

## Quality goal

Make the report sufficient for the operation that consumes it without making
it impersonate a durable knowledge claim. State the subject, inputs or source
state, method, result, and material limits to the degree needed to interpret
or reproduce the output. Record the model and prompt or instruction identity
when an LLM judgment is part of the evidence and the producing workflow does
not already retain them.

`state/` must satisfy the owning workflow's authority, integrity, and cleanup
rules. `retained/` must remain
understandable from a clean checkout without relying on ignored files.

## Titles, descriptions, and exact records

- Use a title that names the analysis, experiment, or result. A title such as
  "Report" does not distinguish the artifact.
- When frontmatter is present, write a retrieval-oriented `description` that
  identifies the subject and why the exact output is retained.
- Frontmatter-free Markdown is permitted for deliberate unstructured output.
- Preserve an exact capture when fidelity is the report's purpose. If a copied
  artifact carries another collection's local type only as captured data, put
  a `.commonplace-validation-ignore` marker at the capture-set root rather than
  presenting that copy as a live typed artifact of this collection.

## Maintenance semantics

- A state producer owns cleanup and states, in the state README, what deleting
  its output loses: nothing unique (rebuild from retained inputs), one paid
  judgment (rerun when needed) or current coverage, an unresolved disposition
  or decision evidence (preserve). Generated state may contain non-reproducible
  judgments or the only current disposition, so Git ignore status never
  licenses deletion.
- A retained report is changed according to its declared role. Correct a
  living report in place; preserve a dated or frozen observation as an exact
  record and create a new observation when the measured state changes.
- Local evidence notes are the one interpreted form `retained/` keeps as
  durable artifacts: a `types/note.md` artifact whose bounded inference
  concerns only Commonplace's own choices or their measured effects, beside
  the raw records it interprets. Its formal edges use this collection's labels
  below. An inference that keeps a free variable belongs in
  `kb/theory/evidence/`.
- If a report develops a transferable claim, binding rule, system premise, or
  unfinished-work lifecycle, extract that content to its proper collection.
  Do not broaden `retained/` into a second notes, reference, instructions, or
  workshop collection.

## Outbound links

Reports may inspect any project surface. Use relative Markdown links for live
navigation and state in prose why the target matters. Inline links may carry
ordinary evidential or procedural context. Footer-shaped formal edges use this
small authorized set:

| label | destinations | reader need |
|---|---|---|
| `derived-from` | sources, external | inspect the source material from which the report was produced |
| `is-evidence-for` | theory, reference, reports | inspect the durable claim, decision, or report record on which this output bears |
| `compares-with` | theory, reference, sources, reports | compare two artifacts on a named shared axis |
| `see-also` | any durable collection, external | inspect useful adjacent context when no stronger relation applies |

The destination collection separately decides whether it may author a
reciprocal edge. A formal edge into this collection targets `retained/`;
`state/` may be mentioned inline only as local operational context.

Tracked library artifacts must not depend on an ignored `state/` file being
present. Summarize the needed evidence in the tracked artifact or
promote the exact report to `retained/` first. Tracked artifacts may cite a
`retained/` report when the exact record is useful to their reader.

## Validation markers

The tracked `.commonplace-validation-ignore` marker at `state/` excludes its
data-bearing subtree from collection-scoped validation. The marker does not
hide files from ordinary discovery, and explicit validation of
one typed report still applies its type contract.

A file under `state/` may declare any valid type spec, including another
collection's local type. Workflows stage candidates there for other
collections, and a candidate must validate against its destination's contract.
The type spec itself stays in the owning collection's `types/` directory.
`retained/` does not share this exception.

## What does not belong here

- A generated explanation or synthesis whose claim should survive the run →
  `kb/theory/` or `kb/reference/` according to its consumer.
- A procedure named "report" because it produces one → `kb/instructions/`.
- Drafts, deliberation, and run traces consumed by an unfinished investigation
  → `kb/work/`.
- External source captures and their durable analyses → `kb/sources/`.
- Build outputs with no report consumer → their build cache, not `kb/reports/`.
